newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower, March holds support.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower, March holds support.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, undermined by a weak physical market, ended lower across the board Thursday in a sluggish session, but March managed to hold above technical support, industry sources said.
March slipped 6.9 cents to close at $2.361 per million British thermal units. April settled 4.6 cents lower at $2.178. Others ended mixed, with some 1999s again up slightly.
"We held the trendline again, but I don't know how much that means. They may try to crash it again tomorrow," said one Midwest trader, noting trendline support for March was in the low-$2.30 area.

While mostly-mild weather this week helped pressure the cash, particularly with eastern stocks 153 bcf or 23 percent over 1996, some said forecasts for colder temperatures next week could stabilize and even firm weekend physical prices.

Technical traders said a March break of the up trendline could set up a test of next support at the Nov 5 low of $2.12. March resistance was seen in the low-$2.50s and then in the $2.70 and $2.80 area.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices skidded 10-15 cents Thursday to the mid-to-high $2.40s. Midcon pipes slipped a similar amount to the mid-to-high $2.30s. New York city gate gas held relatively steady in the low-$3 area, helped by forecasts for colder weather early next week.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 2.3 cents to $2.197. NYMEX said an estimated 21,748 Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 26,887.
NYMEX said 16 Alberta natgas contracts traded, while Permian did not trade Thursday.

On the KCBT, March finished 4.1 cents lower at $2.099, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.8 cents to 26.2 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 88 lots changed hands, down from Wednesday's total of 164.
